reviews.title: gave 1 number to 2+ customers
reviews.body:
gave 1 number to 2+ customers, incredible!

I only found out what'd happened because another person thoughtfully replied to my son, saying that they weren't me & that it seemed as tho his texts hadn't been meant for them but to his mum.
This explained why texts sent to me by both my son & my boyfriend weren't received by me despite their having used Reply, which automatically sends the reply to the same number.  I mean this showed that 
  **either** the other person & I had both been given the same phone number by Lebara, 
  **or** that, if we have separate numbers, texts sent to me are instead going to the other number.
Such mix-ups are absolutely inexcusable.  What if I'd been in need & in danger?  (I've not received texts intended for the other person, so they'd've been OK if in danger.)
  We only found out the above today, 30 Sep, after 3 weeks, & only found out because the other person thoughtfully texted my son to explain that they'd been receiving texts that were clearly not intended for them.
  Meanwhile, I'd obviously been emailing Lebara lots about the service failing to send me the texts that people'd sent me, but Lebara didn't reply at all, except to keep asking, "How did we do?" to which obviously I replied that they didn't "do" at all.
  I find it hard to believe that in this day+age that such mix-ups/glitches can still occur.  I'm also disgusted that Lebara totally ignored all my emails. (I don't/can't call – I did explain this – but even if I could all, some things are clearer by email.)
  I appreciate that Lebara have a brilliant customer rating, which is why I'd chosen them (also cos they use the Vodafone-Three network), but my experience of them is that their product is extremely glitchy to the point of being unuseable & that they couldn't care less about that, nor about their customers.

reviews.title: I’ve been with Lebara for a few months…
reviews.body:
I’ve been with Lebara for a few months now and, as network providers go, they’ve been okay. I haven’t had any issues with connectivity, and the automated emails reminding me to renew for another month have been fine too.

The problem I’ve had, and one I’ve seen mentioned by other customers, is when it comes to claiming a reward. The whole process seems unnecessarily difficult, with confusing information, misleading directions on how to claim and glitches along the way. It honestly feels like they make it so difficult that you eventually just give up.

I originally referred a friend because I was happy with my service and felt confident recommending Lebara. Unfortunately, after this experience, I won’t be referring anyone else. It has really knocked my confidence in the brand. I worry when I want to cancel will they make that hard work too. 

I’ve also tried contacting customer service by phone, only to sit on hold and then have the call disconnect. That was another frustrating and unnecessary waste of my time.

If you’re simply looking for a cheap network that does the basics, Lebara seems to do the job. But based on my experience, I wouldn’t recommend it. The hassle of dealing with issues and trying to claim rewards just isn’t worth it.
